description: Mars Mission Intelligence: Web app for Mars data analysis, interactive maps, and AI science. Looking For: Teammates
summary: Mars Mission Intelligence transforms Martian environmental data into accessible scientific insights. Using real NASA Curiosity rover observations, our platform visualizes weather conditions, identifies unusual environmental readings, predicts temperature trends using machine learning, and provides an AI-powered scientific assistant. Our goal is to make Martian environmental information easier to explore and understand for future missions.
details:
Mars Mission Intelligence is an interactive scientific platform that transforms Martian environmental data into useful insights for Mars exploration.

The platform uses 4,745 cached observations from NASA's Curiosity rover REMS weather feed. It allows users to explore temperature and atmospheric conditions, visualize environmental changes, identify unusual readings using anomaly-detection algorithms, and predict temperature trends using machine learning.

The platform also includes an interactive Martian spatial environment map, a project-defined environmental index called MECI, a Mars Event Replay feature, and an evidence-grounded AI Science Assistant.

Our project aims to make complex planetary science data easier to understand and explore. By combining NASA observations, data visualization, statistical analysis, and machine learning, we hope to support scientific learning and contribute to research tools for future Mars exploration.

What makes our project creative is the integration of several scientific analysis tools into one accessible platform, with an emphasis on data transparency. Real Curiosity observations are clearly distinguished from simulated InSight and MRO demonstration data.

We developed the project using Python, React, TypeScript, FastAPI, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Scikit-learn, and Vite. We also used AI-assisted development tools and an optional Gemini integration for the AI Science Assistant.

Our machine-learning evaluation achieved a 17.8% lower Mean Absolute Error than a simple persistence baseline (3.72°C compared with 4.53°C) on 708 test observations.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, missing observations, model limitations, usability, and transparency. This project is an educational and scientific prototype, not a certified system for astronaut safety or navigation.
